text:
sam-support: Hey team — customer reports intermittent 401s when we validate their signed webhook payloads. Happens ~1-3x/day for a handful of requests. Attaching sample headers/body they shared.

sam-support: ```
POST /webhooks/acme HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
X-Signature: eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImEyYyJ9..(sig)
X-Signature-Format: JWS

{
  "order_id": 1234,
  "status": "paid"
}
```

jen-sre: Do our logs show why verification failed? is it "kid not found" or sig mismatch or expiry?

sam-support: We grab two error samples from edge logs: one says "jws_verify: no matching key for kid a2c" and another shows "token_expired: exp -2" (only by a couple seconds). Both from the same customer account.

ash-runtime: Huh — no matching kid suggests their token used a new key we don't have in cache, but token_expired by 2s smells like clock skew. Can we see the raw JWT payload (decoded)?

sam-support: Posted the decoded payloads (customer sanitized):

sam-support: ```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"a2c"}.
{"iss":"https://id.acme.example","sub":"webhook","exp":1718999999000,"iat":1718999990000}
```

maria-sec: Wait — their exp/iat are in milliseconds (1718999999000). Our validator expects seconds (int seconds since epoch). If we parse that as seconds, exp ~ year 53933 — that'd be fine, but if we coerce to 32-bit int or try to cast/round weirdly it could overflow or be interpreted incorrectly. But token_expired by -2s indicates we DID parse into seconds but got an off-by factor?

ash-runtime: Quick note on our code: we call time.Now().Unix() and compare to int64(claims["exp"]) after type assertion. If their lib encodes exp as float64 with ms, the conversion to int64 will produce 1718999999000 (ms) and now.Unix() is ~1719000001 (s) -> exp >> now so shouldn't be expired. So odd. Unless somewhere we divide by 1000 for other reasons or a JSON decoder returns string and we parse differently.

jen-sre: Another datapoint: our edge logs show JWKS fetches to https://id.acme.example/.well-known/jwks.json returned 200 most times but ~5% of the time returned 429/403 (rate limited) during the customer's key rotation window. Our JWKS cache TTL is 15m and on key-miss we do a cache-refresh attempt but we rate-limit those refreshes to avoid thundering herd. If refresh fails we return kid-not-found.

maria-sec: So hypothesized sequence: customer rotates keys, sends a token signed with new kid. Our cache doesn't yet have it and fetch attempt hit IDP rate limits -> kid-not-found. Separately, some of their tokens contain exp in milliseconds, and our claim-parsing code sometimes coerces floats to seconds incorrectly (we have a conversion path that divides floats >1e11 by 1000 but only in one branch). That could explain intermittent "expired by seconds" errors when different code paths are taken (e.g., different middleware versions on different nodes).

sam-support: Customer says these failures correlate with their key rotation events + our 5xx rate-limiting windows. They can delay rotation by 10m as a workaround. They also mentioned their SDK recently changed to ms timestamps.

ash-runtime: Repro idea: craft a JWT with exp in ms and trigger our verification across a canary fleet where some nodes run older middleware. Also simulate JWKS 429s to reproduce kid-not-found. I can spin up a local proxy that returns 429 for jwks fetches.

jen-sre: Logs to help: from edge (redacted):
```
[2024-07-21T10:12:01Z] verify start kid=a2c req_id=...
[2024-07-21T10:12:01Z] jwks: cache miss, fetching https://id.acme.example/.well-known/jwks.json
[2024-07-21T10:12:02Z] jwks: fetch 429 rate_limited
[2024-07-21T10:12:02Z] verify fail no matching key kid=a2c req_id=...

[2024-07-21T10:12:03Z] verify start kid=a2c req_id=...
[2024-07-21T10:12:03Z] claims parsed exp=1718999999 (seen as seconds) now=1719000001 -> expired_by=-2s
```

maria-sec: Action items I suggest:
- Short-term: treat kid-not-found as a soft-fail: attempt one immediate async jwks refresh and if that fails, enqueue background retry and return 412 (or 202) to customer + advisory, instead of 401, while we refresh.
- Short-term: add a small leeway for exp checks (e.g., 5s) to account for ms/seconds mixed encodings and clock skew.
- Medium-term: harden claims parsing to accept exp/iat as either seconds or milliseconds (detect magnitude > 1e11 -> divide by 1000) and ensure all runtime variants share the same parsing lib.
- Medium-term: exponential backoff + jitter for jwks refreshes and a burst allowance during rotation windows for known IDPs.

ash-runtime: Agreed. I'll open a small PR to normalize exp/iat parsing and add the 5s leeway. jen-sre, can you own the JWKS refresh/ratelimiting change?

jen-sre: Yep. I'll instrument fetch failures and add a temporary elevated-refresh-path for detected rotations (if we see a kid in auth header that we don't have, allow one immediate uncapped fetch). Also add metrics/alerts for jwks 4xx/5xx during rotation.

sam-support: I'll notify the customer of the workaround and ETA: quick fix for parsing/leeway shipped to canary today, jwks-refresh changes planned for tomorrow. I'll include suggested rotation guidance for now. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy started: 1719000200 -> canary cluster (exp/iat normalization + 5s leeway).

maria-sec: Thanks everyone. Please paste PR links here when ready and we'll close the escalation once canary shows no failures for 1 hour.
